subject: Acceptance velocity audit & mitigation tracker
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Hayes <sam.hayes@vanguardhealth.com>, Linda Park <linda.park@vanguardhealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acceptance velocity audit & mitigation tracker

Hi Sam / Linda,

Following our acceptance-window review this morning I ran a quick velocity audit against the MAP milestones you and I agreed to. Short version: the current pace on integration/acceptance tasks is behind the baseline by 11 business days and procurement signals a potential hold next week unless SSO evidence and the final SOC-2 attestation are in place.

I pulled a risk log and a proposed mitigation tracker (attached) with three leveled responses:

- Level 1 (minimal): accelerate bi-weekly integration checkpoint, assign a single technical owner from your side and our side, auto-accept minor verification items for canary.
- Level 2 (moderate): extra Dedicated capacity for two weeks to unblock peak test windows + 10% credit for acceptance delay.
- Level 3 (severe): procurement hold triggers phased go-live and extended acceptance window; requires exec-level credit sign-off.

Action items I recommend now:
1) Please confirm a technical owner from Vanguard for acceptance items by EOD Thursday.
2) Accept the attached updated MAP_v2 milestones (sheet 'MAP_Tracked') so we can commit to an adjusted canary window.
3) If procurement needs evidence earlier, we can arrange an interim SOC-2 evidence bundle export by Friday.

Attachments: [Attachment: MAP_v2.xlsx (Excel, 48KB)], [Attachment: acceptance_audit_notes.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

I'll open a short internal thread with ops/solutions to scope the Dedicated surge option; including Grace on this thread for CS coordination.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — useful summary. We were hoping to avoid increasing spend but the procurement team just flagged the SOC/SSO gap as a showstopper for the current close date. A few notes from our side: 

- We can name a technical owner (I will be point until Linda confirms an infra lead) — I will confirm by Thursday morning.
- Procurement asked whether Redwood can provide a short-term evidence bundle instead of full SOC remediation; they also asked whether you can confirm any credit accommodations if the acceptance window extends.
- Our QA team is asking for a confirmed canary plan (what's included, rollback criteria, and timeline).

On Wed, May 27, 2025 at 9:12 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:

Can you (Marissa/Grace) propose the canary scope and updated MAP milestones so procurement has something formal to review? If procurement approves the evidence bundle instead of the full SOC cadence, we can preserve the original commercial window.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 29 May 2025 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acceptance velocity audit & mitigation tracker

Marissa / Grace — quick ops note after looking at the audit:

Quoted: 
> the current pace on integration/acceptance tasks is behind the baseline by 11 business days

Root cause (short): test environment contention + missing SSO cert and partial test vectors from Vanguard. Proposed mitigation steps:

1) Nightly dedicated test window (12am–4am PT) for two weeks using Dedicated surge (pre-reserved nodes). Ops estimates this will recover ~6–8 business days of velocity.
2) Provide an interim compliance pack (manifest of logs + compressed evidence) this week; Grace, can CS produce the export?
3) Offer a one-time 10% credit on the acceptance milestone's invoiced amount if Vanguard confirms a technical owner within 48 hours and signs the adjusted MAP sheet.

If we proceed with (1)+(2)+(3) we can propose a revised close delta of ~3 business days vs. original baseline (rather than 11). For anything beyond that, we should escalate for exec credit approval.

Marissa —Can you confirm you have procurement conversation notes and that you're ok to request a 10% commercial concession? I'll draft the credit_approval_request.pdf and stack it for Jonas' review.

Thanks,
Karthik
Engineering Manager, Solutions (Redwood Inference)
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 01 Jun 2025 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Acceptance velocity audit & mitigation tracker — escalation note

Forwarding my quick risk note for leadership visibility. Key points: 

- Impact: If procurement refuses interim evidence approval, the deal close shifts by at least 14 business days; this creates downstream cadence conflicts for our onboarding and professional services calendar.
- Severity: Medium-high — financial exposure if we do not grant a concession or provide a hard commitment on Dedicated capacity.
- Recommended immediate actions:
  * Approve the 10% one-time credit on the acceptance milestone (conditional on Vanguard naming a technical owner in 48 hours).
  * Pre-approve allocation of two weeks of Dedicated surge (ops to bill against reserves).
  * Grace to confirm the CS export schedule for interim evidence by EOD Monday.

Jonas attached a draft credit approval request for exec sign-off.

[Attachment: credit_approval_request.pdf (PDF, 24KB)]

On escalation paperwork — Marissa, please confirm you are comfortable asking for the credit and whether you need any additional talking points for procurement. If we don't move, we should set a new public close target and update the MAP so internal teams can re-plan.

Jonas Weber
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 03 Jun 2025 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acceptance velocity audit & mitigation tracker — updated MAP and next steps

Thanks everyone — short update and commitments: 

1) Vanguard named Sam as interim technical owner; Linda to confirm infra lead by Friday.
2) Redwood will produce the interim SOC evidence bundle by Friday 6 June — Grace will coordinate the CS export.
3) Redwood operations will schedule a Dedicated surge window (12am–4am PT) starting Monday 9 June for two weeks; Karthik to confirm node counts by Friday.
4) Redwood will apply a one-time 10% credit to the acceptance milestone invoice conditioned on signed MAP_v2 (attached) and Vanguard naming the final technical owner.

Attached: [Attachment: MAP_v2.xlsx (Excel, 48KB)], [Attachment: credit_approval_request.pdf (PDF, 24KB)]

Next steps (for clarity):
- Sam: confirm infra lead by 06/06 EOD.
- Linda/procurement: review interim evidence bundle once Grace shares and provide written acceptance or list of open items within 48 hours of receipt.
- Redwood (Marissa/Karthik/Grace): deliver evidence bundle, apply credit once MAP_v2 is signed, start Dedicated surge on 09/06.

If procurement approves the interim evidence, we will preserve the original commercial close window and proceed with the planned cutover. If not, I will send an updated MAP public notice with the new close date by EOD Thursday so internal teams have a clear re-baseline.

Appreciate the fast coordination — I will keep this thread as the single source of record for the MAP adjustments and risk log.

Best,
